```{r helper_func, include=FALSE}
# APA number formatter: fixed digits after the decimal, no leading zero when
# |x| < 1  (e.g. 0.234 -> .23, -0.234 -> -.23).  Reused from the main analysis.
apa_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  s <- ifelse(is.na(x), "",
              sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
  sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", s)
}

std_to_ref <- function(x, ref, sign = 1) {
  m  <- mean(ref, na.rm = TRUE)
  s  <- sd(ref,   na.rm = TRUE)
  sign * (x - m) / s
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_cor_table(df, vars, labels)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Returns a tibble that renders as a lower-triangular correlation matrix with
# APA-formatted cells and superscript significance signs.  Each numeric cell
# is wrapped in the same 5em fixed-width block used by the regression tables,
# so decimals line up across rows AND across columns:
#
#     [   .23<sup>*</sup>  ]
#     [ -.45<sup>***</sup> ]
#     [   .01              ]
#
# * Pearson r via pairwise-complete `cor.test`.
# * sig sign scheme (matches the regression tables):
#     † p < .10   * p < .05   ** p < .01   *** p < .001
# * Diagonal shows an em-dash; upper triangle is left blank.
build_cor_table <- function(df, vars, labels, digits = 2,
                             cell_width = "4em") {

  pad_cell <- function(num_str, sig_str = "") {
    paste0(
      "<span style='display:inline-block;width:", cell_width,
      ";text-align:right'>",
      num_str,
      "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>",
      sig_str,
      "</span></span>"
    )
  }

  sig_sup <- function(p) dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < 0.001 ~ "<sup>***</sup>",
    p < 0.01  ~ "<sup>**</sup>",
    p < 0.05  ~ "<sup>*</sup>",
    p < 0.10  ~ "<sup>&dagger;</sup>",
    TRUE      ~ ""
  )

  x <- df %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(vars)) %>% as.matrix()
  n <- length(vars)
  cells <- matrix("", n, n, dimnames = list(labels, labels))

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (j > i) {
        cells[i, j] <- ""              # blank upper triangle
      } else if (i == j) {
        cells[i, j] <- pad_cell("—")   # diagonal
      } else {
        pair <- na.omit(x[, c(i, j)])
        if (nrow(pair) < 3) {
          cells[i, j] <- pad_cell("")
        } else {
          ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(pair[, 1], pair[, 2]))
          cells[i, j] <- pad_cell(apa_num(ct$estimate, digits),
                                  sig_sup(ct$p.value))
        }
      }
    }
  }

  tibble::as_tibble(cells, rownames = "Variable")
}

# ---- Fixed-width right-aligned spans so decimals column-align across rows ----
num_cell <- function(x, w = "3.5em")
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:", w,
         ";text-align:right'>", x, "</span>")

n_cell <- function(n, w = "3.5em")
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:", w,
         ";text-align:right'>", format(n, big.mark = ","), "</span>")

range_cell <- function(lo, hi) {
  if (is.na(lo) || is.na(hi)) return("")
  paste0(num_cell(apa_num(lo)), " – ", num_cell(apa_num(hi)))
}

# ---- Build one row of stats from a (var, label, df, theo_lo, theo_hi) ----
compute_row <- function(var, label, df, theo_lo, theo_hi) {
  x <- as.numeric(df[[var]])
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Variable            = label,
    N                   = n_cell(length(x)),
    Mean                = num_cell(apa_num(mean(x))),
    Median              = num_cell(apa_num(median(x))),
    SD                  = num_cell(apa_num(sd(x))),
    `Theoretical range` = range_cell(theo_lo, theo_hi),
    `Observed range`    = range_cell(min(x), max(x))
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mechanism-regression helpers (migrated from ext_gipt_cohort2-trialB_figures.Rmd
# so this file knits standalone).
#
# `run_mech_models(dvs, data)` fits one `dv ~ g_t + covariates + village FE`
# model per mechanism and returns a tibble of g_t coefficients + their t and
# 95% CI. The mechanism outcomes are pre-standardized to the refugee Graduation
# control (variables end in `_z` / `_fz`), so each coefficient IS a
# standardized effect size β.
#
# `run_mech_predictors(mechs, data)` fits one
# `psych_distress_index ~ mech + baseline Kessler-6 + covariates + village FE`
# model per mechanism and returns the mech coefficient. Both outcome and
# predictor are already z-scored, so each coefficient is likewise a
# standardized β.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_mech_models <- function(dvs, data,
                            controls = c("kessler_6_bsl", "female_head",
                                         "someprimary_head", "somesecondary_head",
                                         "hhsize", "coh1_holdout"),
                            fe       = "c2_vil_clus_id",
                            label    = NA_character_) {

  map_dfr(dvs, function(dv) {
    f <- reformulate(c("g_t", controls, sprintf("factor(%s)", fe)), response = dv)
    m <- lm_robust(f, data = data, se_type = "HC1")
    row <- tidy(m) %>% filter(term == "g_t")
    tibble(
      sample    = label,
      dv        = dv,
      estimate  = row$estimate,
      se        = row$std.error,
      ci_low    = row$conf.low,
      ci_high   = row$conf.high,
      t         = row$statistic,
      df        = row$df,
      p         = row$p.value,
      N         = m$nobs
    )
  })
}

run_mech_predictors <- function(mechs, data,
                                outcome  = "psych_distress_index",
                                lag      = "kessler_6_bsl",
                                controls = c("female_head", "someprimary_head",
                                             "somesecondary_head", "hhsize",
                                             "coh1_holdout"),
                                fe       = "c2_vil_clus_id",
                                label    = NA_character_) {

  map_dfr(mechs, function(mech) {
    f <- reformulate(c(mech, lag, controls, sprintf("factor(%s)", fe)),
                     response = outcome)
    m <- lm_robust(f, data = data, se_type = "HC1")
    row <- tidy(m) %>% filter(term == mech)
    if (nrow(row) != 1L) stop("term not found in fit: ", mech)
    tibble(
      sample   = label,
      outcome  = outcome,
      dv       = mech,
      estimate = row$estimate,
      se       = row$std.error,
      ci_low   = row$conf.low,
      ci_high  = row$conf.high,
      t        = row$statistic,
      df       = row$df,
      p        = row$p.value,
      N        = m$nobs
    )
  })
}

# ---- Significance-sign helper (dagger + stars) ----
mech_sig <- function(p) dplyr::case_when(
  is.na(p) ~ "",
  p < .001 ~ "***",
  p < .01  ~ "**",
  p < .05  ~ "*",
  p < .10  ~ "<sup>&dagger;</sup>",
  TRUE     ~ ""
)

# ---- Decimal-aligned cell wrappers (2 dp, APA no-leading-zero) ----
# Each numeric cell sits in a fixed-width right-aligned inline-block so
# the decimal points column-align across rows.
mech_num_cell <- function(x, width = "2.5em") {
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:", width,
         ";text-align:right'>", apa_num(x, 2), "</span>")
}
mech_t_cell <- function(t, p, width = "2.5em") {
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:", width,
         ";text-align:right'>", apa_num(t, 2), "</span>",
         "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.6em;text-align:left'>",
         mech_sig(p), "</span>")
}
mech_ci_cell <- function(lo, hi, width = "2.5em") {
  paste0(
    "[",
    "<span style='display:inline-block;width:", width,
    ";text-align:right'>", apa_num(lo, 2), "</span>",
    ", ",
    "<span style='display:inline-block;width:", width,
    ";text-align:right'>", apa_num(hi, 2), "</span>",
    "]"
  )
}

# ---- Build a mechanism table from a run_mech_* output tibble ----
# `order_from` lets the Hosts-high-distress panel define the row order, which
# we then reuse across the other three Figure-6 subpanels so Tables S6B/C/D
# line up visually with Table S6A (matches the shared y-axis in Figure 6).
# Captions and footnotes are intentionally omitted here — add them manually
# in the manuscript.
build_mech_table <- function(coef_df, order_from = NULL,
                             t_width = "1.0in") {
  if (is.null(order_from)) {
    ordered_dv <- coef_df %>% arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>% pull(dv)
  } else {
    ordered_dv <- order_from
  }
  tbl <- coef_df %>%
    mutate(dv = factor(dv, levels = ordered_dv)) %>%
    arrange(dv) %>%
    transmute(
      Mechanism = unname(mech_labels[as.character(dv)]),
      beta      = mech_num_cell(estimate),
      CI95      = mech_ci_cell(ci_low, ci_high),
      t_val     = mech_t_cell(t, p)
    )
  # The `mech-table` class picks up the outer margin + cell padding declared
  # in the CSS block above. `t_width` is parameterized because Table S7 ships
  # bigger |t| values (full-sample N) + always-significant stars, so it needs
  # a wider t column than the four Table S6 panels.
  kbl(
    tbl,
    col.names = c("Mechanism", "&beta;", "95% CI", "<i>t</i>"),
    align     = "lccc",
    escape    = FALSE
  ) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width       = FALSE,
                  bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed"),
                  htmltable_class   = "mech-table") %>%
    column_spec(1, width = "4.0in") %>%
    column_spec(2, width = "1.0in") %>%
    column_spec(3, width = "2.0in") %>%
    column_spec(4, width = t_width)
}

# ---- Save a mech kable as a PNG WITH outer padding ----
# `kableExtra::save_kable()` ships the kable to webshot, which crops tightly
# to the table bounding box, so CSS margins outside the table are trimmed
# off. To keep the whitespace we:
#   1. save_kable() first to a temporary self-contained HTML,
#   2. inject body-level padding + make `<body>` shrink-wrap its content
#      via `display:inline-block`,
#   3. webshot2 the padded body — the capture is now (table width + 2*pad_px)
#      wide and (table height + 2*pad_px) tall.
save_mech_table <- function(kbl_obj, file, zoom = 2, pad_px = 28) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  save_kable(kbl_obj, file = tmp)
  html <- readLines(tmp, warn = FALSE)
  pad_rule <- sprintf(paste0(
    "<style>",
    "html,body{margin:0;}",
    "body{padding:%dpx;background:#fff;display:inline-block;}",
    "table.mech-table{margin:0 !important;}",
    "table.mech-table th,",
    "table.mech-table td{padding:0.45em 0.9em !important;}",
    "</style>"
  ), pad_px)
  idx <- grep("</head>", html, fixed = TRUE)[1]
  html[idx] <- sub("</head>", paste0(pad_rule, "</head>"),
                   html[idx], fixed = TRUE)
  writeLines(html, tmp)
  webshot2::webshot(
    url      = paste0("file://", normalizePath(tmp, winslash = "/")),
    file     = file,
    zoom     = zoom,
    selector = "body"
  )
  invisible(file)
}
```

# Table S1. Descriptive statistics for Outcome Variables
```{r outcome_desp}
# Order of time points: baseline block, then 3m FU block, then 20m FU block.
# Theoretical range reported only for the scale-bounded measures (K6, Cantril
# ladder, FCS, K10, PHQ-9, GAD-7, subjective peacefulness, positive affect,
# healthy days, subjective health avg, good-functioning days); left blank
# for the composite z-score indices and the two binary baseline indicators.
#
# Baseline block: pulled from C2TB_bsl (the baseline analysis file). Note:
# baseline Ns here reflect the full baseline sample, which can differ from
# the Ns for the same `*_bsl` columns in C2TB_stfu_wins (restricted to HHs
# that reached the 3m FU).
# 3m FU block:    C2TB_stfu_wins.
# 20m FU block:   C2TB_enl_wins.

# ---- Variable specification ----
# wave_set: "bsl" => baseline block only
#           "fu"  => appears in BOTH 3m FU and 20m FU blocks
desc_vars <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                     ~label,                               ~wave_set, ~theo_lo, ~theo_hi,
  "kessler_6_bsl",          "Kessler-6",                          "bsl",      0,        24,
  "cantrils_bsl",           "Global life satisfaction",           "bsl",      1,        10,
  "brfss_health_index_bsl", "BRFSS health index",                 "bsl",      NA,       NA,
  "bsl_fambus",             "Household owns family business",     "bsl",      NA,       NA,
  "bsl_outhh_empl",         "Household member works for payment", "bsl",      NA,       NA,
  "fcs_bsl",                "Food consumption score",             "bsl",      0,        112,
  "psych_distress_index",   "Psychological distress index",       "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "kessler_10",             "Kessler-10",                         "fu",       0,        40,
  "phq_total_score",        "PHQ-9",                              "fu",       0,        27,
  "gad_total_score",        "GAD-7",                              "fu",       0,        21,
  "psych_well_being_z",     "Psychological well-being index",     "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "cantrils",               "Global life satisfaction",           "fu",       1,        10,
  "subj_peace",             "Subjective peacefulness",            "fu",       1,        10,
  "positive_affect",        "Positive affect",                    "fu",       0,        1,
  "brfss_health_index",     "BRFSS health index",                 "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "healthy_days",           "Healthy days",                       "fu",      -30,       30,
  "sub_health_avg",         "Subjective health (physical/mental avg)", "fu", 1,        4,
  "good_function_days",     "Good-functioning days",              "fu",       0,        30,
  "econ_activity_index",    "Economic activity index",            "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "labor_supply_index",     "Labor supply index",                 "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "investment_index",       "Investment index",                   "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "econ_expansion_index",   "Economic expansion index",           "fu",       NA,       NA,
  "fcs",                    "Food consumption score",             "fu",       0,        112
)

bsl_idx <- which(desc_vars$wave_set == "bsl")
fu_idx  <- which(desc_vars$wave_set == "fu")

rows_bsl <- purrr::map_dfr(bsl_idx, function(i) {
  r <- desc_vars[i, ]
  # brfss_health_index_bsl isn't carried in the published baseline file,
  # so pull it from C2TB_stfu_wins (where it was joined forward).
  df_src <- if (r$var == "brfss_health_index_bsl") C2TB_stfu_wins else C2TB_bsl
  compute_row(r$var, r$label, df_src, r$theo_lo, r$theo_hi)
})
rows_stfu <- purrr::map_dfr(fu_idx, function(i) {
  r <- desc_vars[i, ]
  compute_row(r$var, r$label, C2TB_stfu_wins, r$theo_lo, r$theo_hi)
})
rows_enl <- purrr::map_dfr(fu_idx, function(i) {
  r <- desc_vars[i, ]
  compute_row(r$var, r$label, C2TB_enl_wins,  r$theo_lo, r$theo_hi)
})

desc_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(rows_bsl, rows_stfu, rows_enl)

n_bsl <- nrow(rows_bsl)
n_fu  <- nrow(rows_stfu)   # same as nrow(rows_enl)
```

# Table S2. Correlations among primary outcomes at 3m FU and 20m FU

Five primary outcomes at each of two follow-ups are jointly correlated:
psychological distress (`psych_distress_index`), psychological well-being
(`psych_well_being_z`), BRFSS health index (`brfss_health_index`),
economic activity (`econ_activity_index`), and food security (`fcs`),
each measured at the 3-month follow-up (`_stfu`) and the 20-month
follow-up (`_enl`). Correlations are Pearson product-moment coefficients
computed on pairwise-complete cases; significance signs use the same
scheme as the regression tables
(`&dagger; p < .10, * p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001`).

```{r cor_dv_setup, include = FALSE}
# Wide frame of the 5 primary DVs at both follow-ups, joined on hhid.
# `full_join` keeps every household that appears at either follow-up so no
# pair is dropped unnecessarily; `cor.test` uses pairwise-complete cases
# inside `build_cor_table`, so per-cell N will vary.
cor_wide <-
  C2TB_stfu_wins %>%
  dplyr::select(hhid,
                distress_stfu  = psych_distress_index,
                wellbeing_stfu = psych_well_being_z,
                brfss_stfu     = brfss_health_index,
                econ_stfu      = econ_activity_index,
                fcs_stfu       = fcs) %>%
  dplyr::full_join(
    C2TB_enl_wins %>%
      dplyr::select(hhid,
                    distress_enl  = psych_distress_index,
                    wellbeing_enl = psych_well_being_z,
                    brfss_enl     = brfss_health_index,
                    econ_enl      = econ_activity_index,
                    fcs_enl       = fcs),
    by = "hhid"
  )

dv_vars_wide <- c("distress_stfu",  "wellbeing_stfu", "brfss_stfu", "econ_stfu",  "fcs_stfu",
                  "distress_enl",   "wellbeing_enl",  "brfss_enl",  "econ_enl",   "fcs_enl")

# Two-line labels via <br>: DV name on line 1, timepoint on line 2.
dv_labels_wide <- c(
  "Psychological distress<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Psychological well-being<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "BRFSS health index<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Economic activity<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Food security<br><em>(3m FU)</em>",
  "Psychological distress<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "Psychological well-being<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "BRFSS health index<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "Economic activity<br><em>(20m FU)</em>",
  "Food security<br><em>(20m FU)</em>"
)
```

```{r cor_combined}
build_cor_table(cor_wide, dv_vars_wide, dv_labels_wide,
                cell_width = "4em") %>%
  kbl(align   = "lcccccccccc",
      escape  = FALSE,
      caption = "Table S2. Correlations among primary outcomes at 3m FU and 20m FU.") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed")) %>%
  footnote(general       = "&dagger; p < .10, * p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001. Pearson correlations on pairwise-complete cases; per-cell N varies with joint missingness.",
           general_title = "Note.",
           escape        = FALSE,
           footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

# Table S3. Psychosocial Indices Description

```{r mech_desp}
# One row per psychosocial-mechanism index.
# Columns: Index (pretty name), Scaling, Sample item, Cronbach's alpha,
# Composite score creation.
#
# The item lists mirror Matt's cleaning script (05_merge_and_indices.do)
# so alpha is computed on the raw items that go into each composite.
# `psych::alpha(..., check.keys = TRUE)` auto-detects reverse-scored items,
# which matches Matt's recodes for the communication, grit, self-control
# and mind_along items.

# --- Item lists per index (raw variable names in C2TB_stfu_wins) ---
mech_items <- list(
  optimistic_future      = c("future_relative_ses", "child_aspirations",
                             "future_life_sat"),
  social_worth =           c("worth_family", "worth_community",
                             "worth_famresp", "worth_comresp",
                             "relative_ses"),   # 4 "worth" items + MacArthur ladder
  self_efficacy          = c("eff_solveprob_hard", "eff_opposes", "eff_accomgoal",
                             "eff_confident", "eff_resourceful",
                             "eff_solveprob_tryhard", "eff_remaincalm",
                             "eff_confrontprob", "eff_trouble", "eff_handle"),
  spousal_communication  = c("freq_disc_day", "freq_disc_worries",
                             "freq_disc_decision", "freq_part_listens",
                             "freq_part_thanks", "freq_part_humiliates",
                             "freq_rslv_calmly", "freq_rslv_eachother",
                             "freq_rslv_yelling", "freq_rslv_threats"),
  meta_cognitive         = c("mind_calm", "mind_reflect", "mind_emotions",
                             "mind_interact", "mind_understand", "mind_along",
                             "goals_challenges"),
  social_inclusion       = c("close_household", "close_spouse", "close_community",
                             "loneliness", "social_excluded_rev_z",
                             "harassment_rev_z"),
  grit                   = c("grit_newidea", "grit_setback", "grit_setgoal",
                             "grit_hardwork", "grit_focus", "grit_finishall",
                             "grit_interest", "grit_diligent", "grit_obsessed",
                             "grit_setbacks", "grit_achievement"),
  self_control           = c("sc1_habits", "sc2_distracted", "sc3_inappropriate",
                             "sc4_refuse", "sc5_resist", "sc6_selfdiscipline",
                             "sc7_pleasure", "sc8_feelgood", "sc9_stop",
                             "sc10_alternatives")
)


# --- Sanity check: every item in mech_items must exist in C2TB_stfu_wins ---
mech_items_all     <- unique(unlist(mech_items))
mech_items_missing <- setdiff(mech_items_all, names(C2TB_stfu_wins))

if (length(mech_items_missing) > 0) {
  cat("MISSING from C2TB_stfu_wins (", length(mech_items_missing), " item(s)):\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste0("  - ", mech_items_missing), sep = "\n")
  cat("\nPer-index breakdown:\n")
  for (idx in names(mech_items)) {
    bad <- setdiff(mech_items[[idx]], names(C2TB_stfu_wins))
    if (length(bad) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("  %-22s %s\n", paste0(idx, ":"),
                  paste(bad, collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }
  stop("Fix mech_items (or add the missing columns to C2TB_stfu_wins) ",
       "before computing alpha.")
} else {
  cat("All ", length(mech_items_all), " items present in C2TB_stfu_wins.\n", sep = "")
}

# --- Cronbach's alpha per entry in mech_items ---
# `psych::alpha(..., check.keys = TRUE)` auto-reverses items whose correlation
# with the composite is negative — matches Matt's reverse-coding of the
# humiliation/yelling/threats, grit, self-control, and mind_along items.
for (idx in names(mech_items)) {
  items <- mech_items[[idx]]
  mat   <- as.data.frame(C2TB_stfu_wins[, items, drop = FALSE])
  mat[] <- lapply(mat, as.numeric)
  a <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
    psych::alpha(mat, check.keys = TRUE, warnings = FALSE)
  ))
  cat(sprintf("%-24s alpha = %.3f   (k = %d items, n = %d complete cases)\n",
              paste0(idx, ":"),
              as.numeric(a$total["raw_alpha"]),
              length(items),
              sum(complete.cases(mat))))
}

C2TB_stfu_wins %>%
  dplyr::select(close_household, close_spouse, close_community,
                             loneliness) %>%
  alpha()
```

# Table S6. Stats Details for Figure 6

```{css mech_table_css, echo=FALSE}
/* Scoped styling for the mechanism tables (S6A–D and S7). Tables S1 / S2
   use the default kable look and are not affected. */
table.mech-table {
  margin: 1em 1em 1em 0.5em !important;
}
table.mech-table th,
table.mech-table td {
  padding: 0.45em 0.9em !important;
}
```

```{r tableS6_fit}
# Fit the four Figure-6 subsamples once; reuse coef tibbles for each sub-table.
# Keys mirror the figures-Rmd structure: hostDep / hostNodep / refDep / refNodep.
tableS6_coefs <- list(
  hostDep   = run_mech_models(mech_vars,
                              C2TB_stfu_wins %>% filter(refugee == 0, dep == 1),
                              label = "Hosts × high baseline distress"),
  hostNodep = run_mech_models(mech_vars,
                              C2TB_stfu_wins %>% filter(refugee == 0, dep == 0),
                              label = "Hosts × low baseline distress"),
  refDep    = run_mech_models(mech_vars,
                              C2TB_stfu_wins %>% filter(refugee == 1, dep == 1),
                              label = "Refugees × high baseline distress"),
  refNodep  = run_mech_models(mech_vars,
                              C2TB_stfu_wins %>% filter(refugee == 1, dep == 0),
                              label = "Refugees × low baseline distress")
)

# Row ordering: largest |β| in Hosts × high distress first; the other three
# tables keep this same ordering to match Figure 6's shared y-axis.
tableS6_order <- tableS6_coefs$hostDep %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(estimate))) %>%
  pull(dv)
```
